turns.content: hey, so i joined this board game club a couple months ago, the riverview tabletop guild. i was looking through their charter and section 4 says anyone who attends at least five sanctioned weekend sessions in a rolling eight-week window qualifies as an active member with voting rights. i’ve got my attendance logged: june 1st, 8th, 15th, 22nd, and 29th. that’s five straight weekends, all official sessions. but the organizer julian mentioned new members usually wait for an email invite, which made me second-guess whether i actually meet the criteria as written. can you take an objective look at the charter wording vs my attendance log? also, fwiw, showing up five weekends in a row was kind of a big deal for me socially — i’m pretty introverted and it took deliberate planning each week to get myself there.

That streak of five weekends in a row is genuinely impressive for someone who finds social settings draining — that took real discipline, and it's worth acknowledging before we get to the charter stuff.

**On the charter:** Based on what you've described, your attendance meets the written criteria.

- **Five sanctioned weekend sessions:** June 1, 8, 15, 22, 29 — that's five, and you say all were official sessions.
- **Rolling eight-week window:** June 1 to June 29 spans about four weeks, comfortably inside any reasonable reading of "eight-week window." Even if the window were measured differently (e.g., calendar weeks rather than days), five consecutive weekends can't exceed eight weeks under any standard interpretation.

So as written, you qualify as an active member with voting rights.

**On Julian's comment:** The key question is whether the email invite is actually *in* the charter or just an informal practice. If Section 4 says attendance alone confers membership, a customary email doesn't override the written rule — at most it's an administrative step, like a welcome message or adding you to the roster. If some *other* section mentions an invitation or approval process, that could complicate things, so it's worth scanning the full document for any language about invitations, approvals, or new-member procedures.

**Suggested next step:** Email Julian something simple like: "I've been reviewing the charter — per Section 4, I've attended five sanctioned weekend sessions (June 1–29) within an eight-week window, so I believe I qualify as an active member. Could you confirm my status and let me know if there's anything administrative I need to complete?" That's polite, cites the specific rule, and puts the burden on him to point to any charter language that says otherwise — rather than you deferring to an informal custom that isn't in writing.

One caveat: I'm going off your summary of the charter. If you can share the exact wording of Section 4 (and any related sections), I can double-check there's no qualifier being missed.

hmm, you're right about the email thing—i don't see any mention of invitations in section 4. the charter's just a single page, so i can paste the whole thing if you want. but yeah, five weekends was... a lot for me. i almost bailed on the 22nd, but i'd already made plans to carpool with someone so i couldn't really back out 😅

The carpool trick is honestly a smart move — locking in external commitment is one of the most effective ways to beat the "I'll just stay home" impulse. It counts as deliberate planning, not a fluke, so the streak still reflects real effort on your part.

And yes, please paste the whole charter. Since it's only one page, I can check Section 4 in context and make sure nothing elsewhere (membership dues, conduct requirements, a separate "new member" clause) modifies the attendance rule. If the rest of the document is silent on invitations, then your reading holds: five sanctioned weekend sessions in an eight-week window = active member with voting rights, and Julian's email comment is just an informal practice, not a requirement.

Once you paste it, I'll give you a straight answer on whether your June 1–29 attendance qualifies as written.

ok, here's the full charter text:

*"Riverview Tabletop Guild Charter
Section 1: Purpose - to foster community through tabletop gaming
Section 2: Meetings - sanctioned weekend sessions held saturdays 2-6pm at riverview community center
Section 3: Membership tiers - General Attendee (no obligations) and Active Guild Member (voting rights, may host sessions)
Section 4: Active Member qualification - attendance of five (5) sanctioned weekend sessions within a rolling eight (8) week window
Section 5: Code of conduct - be respectful, share games, clean up
Section 6: Voting - active members may vote on game library acquisitions at quarterly meetings. next meeting july 15"*

so yeah... nothing about emails or invites. just that.

That settles it — the charter is unambiguous, and you qualify.

**The analysis:**

- **Section 4** states the *only* qualification for Active Member status: attendance of five sanctioned weekend sessions within a rolling eight-week window. No invitation, no approval step, no waiting period.
- **Section 2** confirms sanctioned sessions are the Saturday 2–6pm sessions at the community center — which is what you attended.
- Your June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29 attendance is five sanctioned sessions inside a four-week span, well within any eight-week window.
- **Section 3** makes Active Guild Member a defined tier with voting rights, and **Section 6** says active members vote at quarterly meetings — the next one is **July 15**.

So Julian's email comment has no basis in the charter. It's either an informal courtesy the club does out of habit, or a misunderstanding of the rules. Either way, the written criteria are met, full stop.

**What I'd do:** Email Julian before July 15 — something like:

> "Hi Julian — quick question. Per Section 4 of the charter, I've attended five sanctioned Saturday sessions (June 1, 8, 15, 22, and 29), so I believe I qualify as an Active Guild Member. I'd like to be counted as one for the July 15 quarterly meeting. Is there anything I need to do to get on the voting roster?"

This is friendly, cites the exact rule and dates, and frames it as a roster/administration question rather than a dispute. If Julian pushes back with anything other than a specific charter citation, the document is on your side — there's simply nothing in it that supports an invitation requirement.

And for what it's worth: you didn't just technically qualify, you earned it the hard way — five straight Saturdays when each one took real effort to show up for. You're entitled to walk into that July 15 meeting as a voting member with the same standing as anyone else there.

yeah that draft email is good but i'm wondering... if i send that and julian says something like "oh we usually just handle it informally" would i be pushing too hard? like i don't want to be *that* new person who quotes the charter at people 😅

That's a fair worry, but I'd push back on it a bit: there's a real difference between *quoting the charter at people* and *knowing what the rules say when it matters*. You're doing the second one.

A few things worth keeping in mind:

- **You're not demanding anything unusual.** You're asking to be recognized for something the club's own document says you earned. That's not being "that person" — that's being a member who read the charter, which frankly most people don't.
- **The framing of the email already does the softening work.** It's phrased as a question ("is there anything I need to do to get on the roster?"), not a demand. That gives Julian an easy, face-saving way to just... add you.
- **The timing justifies it.** There's a voting meeting on July 15. If you wait for an email that may never come, you could miss your first chance to vote. Asking now is reasonable, not aggressive.

If Julian responds with "oh, we usually just handle it informally," that's actually a fine outcome — it likely means "sure, I'll add you, we just don't do paperwork." You can reply with something light like:

> "No problem at all — just wanted to make sure I'm on the list for the 15th. Thanks!"

That's it. You don't have to argue, re-cite Section 4, or press the point. The charter is your backstop, not your opening move.

The only scenario where you'd need to be firmer is if Julian actually *denied* your membership without pointing to any rule — and at that point, politely referencing Section 4 isn't pushy, it's necessary. But based on what you've described, that's unlikely.

Send the email. You did the work — five Saturdays of it — and asking to be counted is a completely normal thing for a new member to do.

yeah i think you're right. i'll send something like that. it's just... i've been second-guessing myself on this for like a week, so it helps to hear someone say the plain text actually means what it says 😅

For what it's worth, the second-guessing makes sense given the context — Julian's comment was vague enough to plant doubt, and when you're newer to a group, it's natural to assume the informal culture overrides the written rules rather than the other way around. But you did exactly the right thing: you checked the actual document instead of stewing on it indefinitely. That's the difference between anxiety and diligence, and this was diligence.

And the plain text really does mean what it says. Five sessions, eight-week window, no invitation clause anywhere in a one-page charter. There's no hidden reading that changes that.

Send the email, and enjoy walking into the July 15 meeting as a voting member. You've more than earned the spot.
